evidence.fitness: Job: a researcher or planner asking whether a fundamental price model is good enough to value a heat store against a heat pump. The code is runnable and reusable within the repo, and the qualitative split (a model can schedule a store but cannot decide a margin smaller than its level error) is useful. As research it is a small step: the scheduling result restates the known finding that arbitrage value is robust to imperfect price forecasts because ranking hours matters more than level (Sioshansi et al. 2009 recover most of perfect-foresight value with simple backcasts; Walawalkar et al. 2007; Mokrian & Stephen 2006), and the level-error point is the standard limit of residual-load / merit-order fundamental models (Kallabis et al. 2016); none is cited, though the README does not claim novelty explicitly. The 'modelled price' is in-sample for later years (LOYO), so it is not the forecast a decision would use; the true forecast is left to Next step 3. Five correlated years, no significance. Not in any programme in research/PROGRAMMES.md.
evidence.domain: Departures a reviewer would flag: (a) the store pays for heat from ambient (10 C) to 500 C every cycle (energy-thermal-cost/cost.py:96,101, used 'exactly' per README:22), but it only discharges to the 100 C cut, so the 10-100 C heat is re-bought each cycle; recharge from the cut needs usable_full_kwh = 0.816 x heat_in_kwh, so the energy bill is overstated 22.5%. Recomputed with that correction (B x 400/490 on the fitted linear cost), the house weekly real-price diff becomes -0.012/-0.012/-0.013/+0.001/-0.009 instead of -0.004/-0.005/-0.005/+0.011/-0.000: the store wins weekly cycling in 4 of 5 years with a tie in 2018, and the resid model then agrees in 2 of 5 (not 0); daily stays 5/5. The headline's 'weekly margin -0.005 to +0.011' is mostly this accounting. (b) Constant COP 3.6 for an air-source pump paid at the flat Nov-Mar mean, no temperature dependence or hourly load weighting (favours the pump in cold hours, and ignores that the pump could also shift load). (c) The store buys the cheapest quarter of every window of the year while heat is wanted in winter; from the raw prices the Nov-Mar daily cheapest quarter differs from the year-round one by -0.0036 to +0.0008 (2018 -0.0036), comparable with the weekly margin. (d) Price-taker only, wholesale, no levies or network charges, stated. The dispatch rule itself is the LP optimum for the stated charger (checked).

defects.what: The inherited cost model bills the store for heat from ambient (10 C) to 500 C every cycle although it only discharges to the 100 C cut, overstating the store's electricity per cycle by 22.5% (usable_full/heat_in = 0.816). Corrected, the house weekly real-price margin is -0.013 to +0.001 (store wins 4 of 5) rather than -0.005 to +0.011, so the headline weekly finding mostly reflects this accounting; not disclosed in Limitations

Core logic untested: 4 of 6 seeded mutants survive, including removing the leave-one-year-out holdout (the design choice the paper rests on), the merit constant, the heat-pump price path, and the run.py store-price window; no test covers experiments/run.py or pins any results.txt number

Nearest prior work uncited: arbitrage value under imperfect price forecasts (Sioshansi et al. 2009; Walawalkar et al. 2007; Mokrian & Stephen 2006) already shows ranking-hours robustness, and residual-load fundamental price models (Kallabis et al. 2016) are known to miss the level; the scheduling result is presented without that context, and the LOYO 'model' is in-sample for later years
'the pump wins in all five years, against two in the real series': the real series has one pump win (2018) and one tie (2019)
Lede 'wrong in sign in 5 of 5 years': 2019 real -0.0005 and modelled -0.0097 share a sign; 4 of 5 are opposite-sign, the fifth a tie miss (also research/README.md:971)
Run time 'about 20 s' / '20 s'; measured 42 s (3.11) and 48 s (3.13); and results differ by 1e-4 in 4 lines on Python >= 3.12 (exact 0.01825 rounding boundary under compensated sum())
Tests are pytest-only and need the pyproject pythonpath; `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` runs nothing and research CI runs no project tests, so no check ever runs them

Store priced on the cheapest quarter of every window of the year while the pump pays the Nov-Mar mean; the heat is wanted in winter. Nov-Mar-only daily cheapest quarter differs by -0.0036 to +0.0008, comparable with the weekly margin; constant COP 3.6 with no temperature dependence

verdict: A tidy, reproducible follow-on whose stored numbers are right for the model as written: the experiment reproduces byte-for-byte on Python 3.11 (4 cells off by 1e-4 on 3.13 at an exact rounding boundary), and my own isotonic fit, window ranking, LP dispatch and annuity reproduce sections A, D, E, the heat-pump cost and the house verdict counts. It misses the bar on verification (4 of 6 seeded mutants survive, including removing the leave-one-year-out holdout) and on claims (two small misstatements of its own table and a stale run time). The worst problem is inherited: the cost model bills the sand store for heat from 10 C each cycle though it only discharges to 100 C, overstating its electricity by 22.5%; corrected, the store wins weekly cycling in 4 of 5 years, so the 'marginal weekly verdict' at the heart of the headline is largely an accounting artefact. The scheduling finding is the known robustness of arbitrage to forecast error (Sioshansi et al. 2009), uncited.
